text:
maria (sre): FYI team — short summary + policy change after last night's graceful-degradation event in control plane. TL;DR: routing tier throttled for ~22m, p99 increased ~180ms, no data loss.

sre-bot: Incident detected: controlplane-router-eu-west High p99 2026-03-22T03:07Z -> auto-fallback triggered to quantized-1 models.

maria (sre): Timeline: 03:05 automatic backpressure hit after a k8s node reboot cascade; 03:07 routing queued, 03:08 canary fallback kicked, 03:30 full routing restored.

tony (sre): Root cause: kubelet restart timing + soft-preempt interrupts on GPU-side path. We saw slow drain of long-lived connections into router and our control plane rate limiter amplified bursts.

jess (prod): Noted a few customer error spikes in Grafana — alerted by posthog dashboards. Did we send any outbound notices?

maria (sre): We sent a status page update at 03:20 with scoped impact to EU customers. No SLA credits expected per current policy, but this prompted policy review.

kai (runtime): Mitigation applied: 1) lowered control-plane concurrency headroom for 10s bursts, 2) enabled shorter kv-cache eviction during drains, 3) tuned soft-preempt backoff to 250ms. Rollout 03:25 -> 03:40.

tony (sre): Action items we agreed in post-incident chat:
- Immediate: add a small circuit-breaker that rejects >5k inflight control-plane requests from same AZ to avoid feedback loops. (owner: tony)
- Near-term: autoscaler cooldown bump from 30s -> 90s for router ASG to avoid simultaneous node restarts. (owner: kai)
- Policy: change SLO burn handling for graceful-degradation events — see below. (owner: maria)

jess (prod): Request: add a product-facing note template we can use when fallbacks to quantized models change outputs subtly. Some customers noticed minor tokenization drift.

maria (sre): New policy summary (effective immediately):
- Define "graceful-degradation" window: any automated fallback invoked by control-plane routing for capacity/reliability reasons will be classified separately from "partial outage".
- Operationally, we will not auto-escalate to incident if user-visible error-rate stays <1% and response completeness is preserved.
- If SLO p99 breach is due to routing-induced backpressure and duration >15min, we will schedule a postmortem and a corrective mitigation within 72h.
- For fallbacks that switch model variants (e.g., to quantized or smaller architectures), product must be notified within 30 minutes.

tony (sre): Rationale: this lets us focus on durable fixes rather than paging for short controlled degradations. It also requires more proactive customer comms when quality may differ.

jess (prod): Agreed. I'll draft the 30-minute notification template and a short FAQ about quantized fallbacks.

kai (runtime): Side note: we should add a synthetic test that simulates node-reboot + soft-preempt interaction weekly. I'll schedule a canary test and link results to console.

maria (sre): For transparency, we'll add a short entry to the Reliability Playbook and update the alerting runbook to include the new circuit-breaker threshold.

oncall-prod: Quick question — will Dedicated customers see a different policy? We need to ensure SLA language covers this classification.

maria (sre): Good call. Dedicated customers are exempt from automatic fallbacks by default; any fallback there requires explicit approval from the customer's safety gate or a configured fallback agreement. We will reach out to account mgmt to confirm contracts.

tony (sre): I'll create the GH issue with the checklist and link runbooks: https://git.company/reliability/issues/4321 (will add owners + due dates).

maria (sre): Recap: policy change published to internal playbook, triage checklist + circuit-breaker PR coming, product to prepare customer template. If anyone sees missing items call them out here. :thumbsup:

jess (prod): Looks good. I'll sync with sales/support on wording.

kai (runtime): Adding the synthetic to the calendar now.

sre-bot: Scheduled: circuit-breaker rollout canary starts 2026-03-24T02:00Z.

maria (sre): Thanks team — closing thread. We'll post the final playbook link in #eng-sre once merged.
